Metacommunity dynamics from growth rates

Source: R/dynamics.R
mc_dynamics.Rd

The engine of simulate_metacommunity(), for users who want to supply their own growth rates (e.g. responses to several environmental variables).

Usage

mc_dynamics(
  r,
  alpha,
  dispersal,
  n_steps = 1000,
  seed_steps = seq(10, 100, 10),
  seed_mean = 0.5,
  disp_matrix = NULL,
  record_steps = NULL,
  sites = NULL,
  species = NULL,
  extirpation = 0,
  pool = NULL,
  initial = NULL,
  immigration = c("poisson", "multinomial")
)

Arguments

r

Sites x species matrix of density-independent growth rates, or a function of the time step that returns such a matrix.

alpha

Competition matrix from competition_matrix(). Species are matched to the rows of traits by name, or by position if alpha has no names.

dispersal

Emigration probability, one value or one per species.

n_steps

Number of time steps.

seed_steps

Steps at which individuals are added during colonisation.

seed_mean

Mean number of individuals of each species added to each site at each seeding step (and at the start).

disp_matrix

Row-stochastic dispersal matrix (sites x sites), or NULL for uniform dispersal.

record_steps

Optional steps at which abundances are recorded.

sites, species

Optional names of sites and species.

extirpation

Probability that a population is lost at each time step, one value or one per species.

pool

Optional matrix (sites x species), logical or 0/1, with the sites where each species can occur.

initial

Optional matrix (sites x species) of abundances or 0/1 presences at the start, only where pool allows.

immigration

How emigrants reach other sites on spatially explicit landscapes: "poisson" (the default, as in the code of Thompson et al. 2020) or "multinomial", which conserves them. Spatially implicit landscapes are always multinomial.

Value

List with abundance and history, as in simulate_metacommunity(), and pool as a logical matrix, or NULL without it.

Examples

set.seed(1)
# one species alone converges to (r - 1) / alpha = (5 - 1) / 0.05 = 80
out <- mc_dynamics(matrix(5, 20, 1), matrix(0.05), dispersal = 0, n_steps = 200)
mean(out$abundance)
#> [1] 78.05
